pages.title: Modular Form
pages.text: A function on the complex upper half-plane with so much symmetry that it is almost forced to be what it is. Modular forms connect primes, elliptic curves and string partition functions, and Wiles used them to prove Fermat's Last Theorem. This one is a slowly turning tiling of curved triangles.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Combining a Fourier series with primes on the complex plane, I hoped for a function whose coefficients counted something arithmetic. The Analytic Continuator returned one invariant under the whole modular group, with prime patterns hiding in its expansion.
